utterances.text: I'm EMS, I'm also your facilitator. Some disbelief will be suspended. When I ask you guys to intubate with the LMA, just bag or verbalize bagging, when you're giving meds verbalize the meds.

So this woman is a 57-year-old woman who has emphysema and is on oxygen at home. Her family states that the patient has been ill with nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea for several days. In the past 48 hours she's been unable to eat or drink anything. Today she had more trouble breathing than usual and breathing has gradually worsened. She was found by EMS unresponsive and cyanotic at home. We found her in a hospital-type bed and she appeared to be non-responsive. We started CPR and we placed an IV. Her initial vitals, she had a heart rate of 116, respiratory rate of zero, there was no pulse, no oxygen, and her heart rhythm was sinus tachycardia with a PEA. And yes, please assign yourself roles and begin.
Okay, you can do compressions, I'll do airway, meds, I'll be the provider.
So compressions... start compressions.

So we knew she was in PEA when she came in. We don't have an airway, so we want to get an airway. She's currently in PEA still, so we can't shock. We need to push 1 of epi while we're getting the airway.
I'm going to give meds, 1 milligram of epi.
Okay, so 1 of epi's given, we have our airway, we're currently bagging, we're doing CPR. Airway's in.

So we know that she was found unresponsive, she has a history of emphysema, she wears oxygen at home we know about. She's in PEA so we can rule out other things that we think's happening. As far as H's and T's, she could be hypoxic, she could have any type of clot or thrombus with her emphysema breathing history, PE. Does she have a cardiac history?
And she was having diarrhea before... so that makes sense for electrolyte derangements.
Maybe we could listen to lung sounds to confirm placement.
All right, listening... You hear bilateral breath sounds.
We can say it's about two minutes, so let's do a pulse check and see where rhythm's at. Does she have a pulse?
You do not feel a pulse.
Continue compressions, she's still in PEA. We can give another push of epi.
Gave epi.
Can we get a point-of-care glucose? We don't have labs back, but your point-of-care glucose is within normal range.
We can do like CBC, CMP, I would do a troponin, do an ABG and just see what her oxygen status was before, do a D-dimer.
Could do an amp of bicarb, I'm sure she's got some acidosis going on. It's about two minutes, we can check a pulse again. Do we have a pulse?
You guys have a pulse. So now her repeat vitals are she is tachycardic to 110, blood pressure is 95 over 77, respiratory rate 14, SpO2 is 94, and her PCO2 is 40. Normal sinus rhythm.

We can give fluids, she's dehydrated most likely... We'll do the fluids see if that improves it. Pulm, cardiology should be consulted. I would get an EKG, CT head, chest X-ray to confirm the ET tube and everything.

case_fields.other_med_considered_list: Sodium bicarbonate (discussed at 04:05 and 05:51), IV fluids (ordered post-ROSC at 06:33)
case_fields.technical_comments: Patient arrived in PEA arrest (01:02). Roles were assigned immediately and chest compressions started at 01:20 (18s after handoff). Non-shockable PEA rhythm was accurately recognized (01:23). First dose of Epinephrine 1 mg IV was administered at 01:45 and supraglottic airway (LMA) placed at 01:50, confirmed via bilateral breath sounds at 03:24. Second pulse/rhythm check at 03:54 showed persistent PEA with a 5s pause; Epinephrine #2 was given at 04:04. Reversible causes (hypoxia, PE/thrombosis, electrolyte derangement/dehydration, hypoglycemia, acidosis) were thoroughly discussed. Third pulse check at 06:04 identified ROSC (06:09), followed by post-ROSC IV fluid orders, 12-lead ECG, chest X-ray, and specialty consults.
case_fields.feedback_narrative:
Chronological Resuscitation Review:
- 01:02 Patient handoff completed; team leader immediately assigned compressor, airway, and medication roles.
- 01:20 Chest compressions initiated promptly (18 seconds from scenario start) and PEA rhythm recognized (01:23).
- 01:45 Epinephrine 1 mg IV #1 administered with closed-loop confirmation; LMA airway placed at 01:50.
- 01:59–03:10 Team leader and team members systematically reviewed H's and T's (hypoxia, pulmonary embolism, dehydration/electrolyte abnormalities from diarrhea).
- 03:24 Airway placement confirmed via bilateral auscultation following prompt from the compressor.
- 03:54–03:59 First 2-minute rhythm/pulse check performed with a brief (<6s) compression pause; persistent PEA identified.
- 04:04 Epinephrine 1 mg IV #2 administered immediately after pulse check; point-of-care glucose checked (04:20).
- 06:04–06:09 Second 2-minute pulse check performed; ROSC achieved and post-arrest care (IV fluids, labs, ECG, CXR, consults) initiated.
case_fields.team_general_comments: Clear, calm leadership by the team leader with strong input from the compressor and airway/med team members. Closed-loop communication was used for Epinephrine administrations, though sodium bicarbonate was suggested twice (04:05, 05:51) without a definitive directive or confirmation of administration. Compressor fatigued slightly in the final minute before ROSC without a role switch.

done_well.title: Rapid CPR Initiation, Rhythm Recognition & Early Epinephrine
done_well.detail: Following EMS handoff at 01:02, the team assigned roles and began chest compressions within 18 seconds (01:20), immediately recognized PEA as a non-shockable rhythm (01:23), and administered the first dose of 1 mg IV Epinephrine at 01:45.
done_well.evidence_quote: So compressions... start compressions... She's currently in PEA still, so we can't shock. We need to push 1 of epi.

done_well.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Reversible Causes (H's & T's)
done_well.detail: Between 01:59 and 04:30, the team actively synthesized the patient's history of emphysema and 48 hours of GI losses to evaluate hypoxia, pulmonary embolism, electrolyte derangements, acidosis, and hypoglycemia (checking POC glucose at 04:10).
done_well.evidence_quote: As far as H's and T's, she could be hypoxic, she could have any type of clot or thrombus... And she was having diarrhea before, so that makes sense for electrolyte derangements.

done_well.title: Proactive Cross-Monitoring by Compressor
done_well.detail: While performing chest compressions, the compressor actively contributed to clinical safety by prompting bilateral lung auscultation to confirm airway placement (03:11) and requesting a point-of-care glucose check (04:10).
done_well.evidence_quote: Maybe we could listen to lung sounds to confirm placement... Can we get a point-of-care glucose?

areas_for_improvement.title: Unresolved Medication Suggestions (Sodium Bicarbonate)
areas_for_improvement.detail: The team leader mentioned 'we could give bicarb' at 04:05 and 'could do an amp of bicarb' at 05:51, but phrased them as tentative thoughts rather than directed orders, resulting in no verbal confirmation or administration by the medication nurse.
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: Address medication orders to a specific team member by name/role with an explicit dose and route, and require verbal read-back and completion confirmation.
areas_for_improvement.evidence_quote: Could do an amp of bicarb, I'm sure she's got some acidosis going on.

areas_for_improvement.title: Single Compressor Across Entire Arrest Without Rotation
areas_for_improvement.detail: A single team member performed continuous chest compressions from 01:20 to 06:04 (nearly 5 minutes across two full 2-minute cycles) without switching compressors during the 03:54 pulse check.
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: Rotate the compressor role at every 2-minute rhythm/pulse check to prevent compressor fatigue and maintain optimal compression depth and recoil.
areas_for_improvement.evidence_quote: Does she have a pulse? You do not feel a pulse. Continue compressions.

areas_for_improvement.title: Delayed Auscultation After Airway Placement
areas_for_improvement.detail: Although the LMA airway was placed and bagging began at 01:50, bilateral breath sound auscultation to confirm placement was not performed until 03:24 (94 seconds later).
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: Confirm advanced airway placement immediately upon insertion using bilateral chest auscultation and continuous waveform capnography.
areas_for_improvement.evidence_quote: We have our airway, we're currently bagging (01:50)... Maybe we could listen to lung sounds to confirm placement (03:11).
